title: Learning Planning Budgets in Real-Time RL
claim: A learned gate picks a planning budget, then cheap reflex actions run while a slower planner improves its action in parallel.
layout: Top gate-to-reflex row, bottom timeline of states with growing trees, left-to-right
description: The figure is a pipeline diagram using Pac-Man as the example. At top left, a cartoon robot labeled π_gate observes the state s_t and decides a budget, shown as a blue arrow reading k = 4. A dotted box at top right shows the reflex rollout. The states s_t, s_{t+1} and s_{t+2} are linked by blue arrows, with π_reflex producing actions a1, a2 and a3. This ends in a green-outlined s_f, labeled as the initial state of the plan. Below, a row of four Pac-Man game frames runs from s_t to s_{t+3} = s_f, joined by action arrows. Under the frames, three MCTS trees rooted at green s_f grow wider. A large green arrow on the right leads to the final action a_f. Pale blue and green colors carry the flow, and monospace text labels each stage.
caption: Given the current state, the gating policy chooses whether to react immediately or spend time planning, selecting the number of timesteps $k$ over which to plan. The agent then takes $k{-}1$ committed actions using $\pi_{\mathrm{reflex}}$ ($\pi_{\mathrm{0}}$) while MCTS plans, and finally executes the planned action.
abstract: Deliberating takes time. In real-time settings, that time is not free. Standard reinforcement learning (RL) sidesteps this as the environment waits indefinitely for the agent's decision. Instead, we study real-time RL environments where the environment progresses while waiting for the agent's action. Building on prior real-time formalizations, we introduce variable-delay real-time RL, where the agent chooses how long to deliberate at each decision point since the environment progresses. For the planning agents we use, the right delay is state-dependent, and naively planning how long to plan can paralyze the agent. We instead approach this setting by training a lightweight gating policy on top of a planner to select state-dependent planning budgets. Across real-time Pac-Man, Tetris, Snake, Speed Hex, and Speed Go, our gating policy outperforms fixed-budget and heuristic baselines, and transfers to a real-time setup where the environment and agent run on two different GPUs.
